title: Residue coefficient restriction and the ambient dualizing object
statement:
Let $F$ be a separably closed field of characteristic $p$, $Z$ a separated finite-type $F$-scheme [def-kun-separably-closed, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and $A=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E^n)$, $n\geq1$, with $\ell\ne p$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Put $k_E=\mathcal O_E/(\varpi_E)$ and let $\rho:A\to k_E$ be reduction. On the ordinary small etale module derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], let $\operatorname{Res}_\rho$ denote termwise restriction of the coefficient action. Let $a_Z:Z\to\operatorname{Spec}F$, and let $a_{Z,A}^{\times}$ and $a_{Z,k_E}^{\times}$ be the ordinary compact-support right adjoints [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint]. Write $\omega_{Z,A}=a_{Z,A}^{\times}A$ and $\omega_{Z,k_E}=a_{Z,k_E}^{\times}k_E$. There is an isomorphism in $D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},k_E)$
$$R\mathcal Hom_A((k_E)_Z,\omega_{Z,A})\simeq\omega_{Z,k_E},$$
where the $k_E$-action on the left is precomposition. For every $M\in D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},k_E)$ there is a natural isomorphism in $D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$
$$R\mathcal Hom_A(\operatorname{Res}_\rho M,\omega_{Z,A})\simeq\operatorname{Res}_\rho R\mathcal Hom_{k_E}(M,\omega_{Z,k_E}).$$
Here derived internal Hom is [def-pur-derived-internal-hom]; no boundedness, constructibility or finite-Tor condition on $M$ is imposed.

source.place: Agent coefficient-coinduction lemma for the coefficient devissage in Remark 3.3 / Theorem 5.1 (local PDF WANTED); ordinary derived coextension model: WeilConjectures/SixFunctors/Etale/Derived/CoextendScalars.lean, lines 55--95; the coefficient-coinduction argument is written in report.md and is not claimed to be a theorem of that source file.

proof.text: Write $k=k_E$, $\pi=\varpi_E$, and $U_T=\operatorname{Res}_\rho$ on the small etale site of any scheme $T$. By [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars] its underlying abelian sheaf is unchanged; kernels and cokernels are unchanged by [lem-weil-pbc-module-sheaves-colimits-forgetful], so $U_T$ is exact. For an $A_T$-module sheaf $J$, put $C_TJ=\ker(\pi:J\to J)$. This is a $k_T$-module: a local lift $a$ of a residue scalar acts by $a$, independently of the lift because $\pi C_TJ=0$. Evaluation at $1$ gives $\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(k_T,J)\cong U_TC_TJ$: its inverse sends a section $x$ annihilated by $\pi$ to $(\bar a\mapsto ax)$. These formulas are defined on every slice site and commute with restriction [def-pur-sheaf-hom]. Every $A_T$-linear map $U_TL\to J$ has image in $C_TJ$ since $\pi L=0$, and is then $k_T$-linear. Factoring through this kernel and composing with its inclusion are inverse natural operations. Thus $U_T\dashv C_T$, with the precomposition $k_T$-action specified in the item.

For $N\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ choose a K-injective representative $I$ using [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Since $U_T$ is exact, the adjunction just constructed and [lem-weil-pbc-right-adjoint-preserves-kinjective] show that $C_TI$ is K-injective over $k_T$. Define $H_TN=Q_k(C_TI)$, with maps computed on the homotopy category of K-injectives. This is independent of the chosen resolution: [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] identifies that category with the derived category and says that a quasi-isomorphism between K-injectives is a homotopy equivalence; any additive $C_T$ preserves the homotopy equation. The evaluation identification of Step 1 gives
$$U_TH_TN=Q_A\mathcal Hom^\bullet_{A_T}(k_T[0],I)=R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(k_T,N).$$
Here [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] supplies the K-injective computation. The complex $C_TI$, with its residue action, is also the asserted $k_T$-valued model of this derived Hom. No resolution of $k_T$ as a perfect $A_T$-module is used.

The same kernel-factorization formula, applied degreewise, is a bijection between chain maps $U_TL^\bullet\to I$ and chain maps $L^\bullet\to C_TI$, and between their chain homotopies. Indeed all differentials are linear, so factoring a map through the kernel commutes with the two sides of $df=fd$ and of $f-g=dh+hd$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-hom-derived] to the K-injective targets $I$ over $A_T$ and $C_TI$ over $k_T$. For every unbounded $L\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},k)$ this gives natural bijections
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k_T)}(L,H_TN)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(k_T)}(L^\bullet,C_TI)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{K(A_T)}(U_TL^\bullet,I)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_T)}(U_TL,N).$$
Thus $U_T\dashv H_T$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories.

source.place: Tag 070I (lemma-K-injective): computation of derived Hom into a K-injective; degreewise adjunction expanded explicitly

proof.text:
For any representative $L^\bullet$ of $L\in D(T_{\mathrm{et}},k)$, kernel factorization on every slice gives an isomorphism of sheaves
$$\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(U_TL^i,I^j)\cong U_T\mathcal Hom_{k_T}(L^i,C_TI^j).$$
The forward map factors through $\ker\pi$; the inverse composes with its inclusion. Products of these inverse maps in total degree $r$ identify the Hom-complex terms $\prod_i\mathcal Hom(U_TL^i,I^{i+r})$. For a homogeneous map $f$ of degree $r$, both differentials are $d_If-(-1)^rf d_L$ [def-pur-hom-complex]; each summand factors through $C_TI$, so these degreewise identifications commute with the differential, including its sign. Because $I$ and $C_TI$ are K-injective, [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] now gives
$$R\mathcal Hom_{A_T}(U_TL,N)\cong U_TR\mathcal Hom_{k_T}(L,H_TN).$$
The inverse maps commute with precomposition in $L$ and postcomposition in $I$. Passing through the K-injective resolution identifications makes the isomorphism natural in both derived variables. This is an isomorphism of $A_T$-complexes, with the action on the right restricted through $\rho$.

proof.text: Put $s=\operatorname{Spec}F$ and $a=a_Z$. A field has only the ideals $0$ and $F$, so $s$ is Noetherian, quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Choose a compactification $Z\xrightarrow{j}\overline Z\xrightarrow{r}s$ by [thm-nagata-compactification]. Both $Z$ and $\overline Z$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], since $a$ is finite type and $r$ is proper, hence finite type. Use this same compactification for both coefficient rings, so the functors in [def-amb-etale-compact-support] are $Ra_{!,A}=Rr_{*,A}j_{!,A}$ and $Ra_{!,k}=Rr_{*,k}j_{!,k}$. At the presheaf level [def-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero], $j_{p!}U_Z=U_{\overline Z}j_{p!}$: on an object factoring through $Z$ both sides have the same sections with restricted action, and otherwise both are zero. Sheafification has the same underlying abelian sheaf for both coefficient actions [def-weil-presheaf-modules-sheafification]; the unique extended action is its restriction along $\rho$. Hence $j_{!,A}U_Z\cong U_{\overline Z}j_{!,k}$, on sheaves and termwise on complexes.

source.place: Tags 03DI (extension by zero), 03CY (sheafification of module presheaves); compactification and Noetherian hypotheses as in the cited nodes

proof.text:
For $T=\overline Z,s$, the identity geometric morphism with ring map $A_T\to k_T$ is a morphism of ringed topoi $(T_{\mathrm{et}},k_T)\to(T_{\mathrm{et}},A_T)$ whose module direct image is $U_T$. Its derived direct image is still termwise $U_T$ because it is exact (Step 1). The two factorizations
$$(\overline Z_{\mathrm{et}},k)\to(\overline Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)\to(s_{\mathrm{et}},A),\qquad (\overline Z_{\mathrm{et}},k)\to(s_{\mathrm{et}},k)\to(s_{\mathrm{et}},A)$$
are the same ringed-topos morphism: direct image is ordinary $r_*$ with $A$ acting through $\rho$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] to each factorization, using the small-site universe of the ordinary derived categories. It gives $Rr_{*,A}U_{\overline Z}\cong U_sRr_{*,k}$ on all unbounded complexes. Compose this with Step 5 and the definition [def-amb-etale-compact-support] to obtain
$$Ra_{!,A}U_Z\cong U_sRa_{!,k}.$$
All these comparisons are natural: they are respectively the derived composition comparisons and the identity on the extension-by-zero presheaves.

source.place: Tag 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition), applied to the two coefficient/geometric factorizations

proof.text:
Compute $H_s(A_s)$. By [lem-kun-0ezp], every object of $s_{\mathrm{et}}$ is a disjoint union of copies of $s$. The sheaf axiom identifies the values of a module sheaf on such a union with the product of its sections on the copies. Thus evaluation at $s$ and the constant-module sheaf functor are inverse exact equivalences between $A_s$-module sheaves and $A$-modules; the same argument applies to $k$. By [lem-weil-coefficient-frobenius], $A=\mathcal O_E/(\pi^n)$ is injective over itself. Consequently $A_s[0]$ is K-injective by [lem-weil-pbc-bounded-below-injectives-kinjective], so $H_s(A_s)$ is $C_s(A_s)[0]$, corresponding to $\operatorname{Ann}_A(\pi)$. By the DVR property in [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr],
$$\operatorname{Ann}_{\mathcal O_E/(\pi^n)}(\pi)=(\pi^{n-1})/(\pi^n).$$
Indeed $\pi x\in(\pi^n)$ if and only if $x\in(\pi^{n-1})$ by cancellation in the domain $\mathcal O_E$. Multiplication by $\pi^{n-1}$ gives a $k$-linear isomorphism $k\to\operatorname{Ann}_A(\pi)$: it is onto by that equality, and its kernel is $(\pi)$ by the same cancellation. Therefore $H_s(A_s)\cong k_s$ in $D(s_{\mathrm{et}},k)$. This also covers $n=1$, where the map is the identity.

source.place: Finite coefficient self-injectivity; agent socle calculation using the DVR property; etale-cohomology.tex Tag 0EZP for the point site

proof.text:
The ambient compact-support right adjoints in [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint] apply: $A,k$ are finite, and Step 5 supplied compactifications between Noetherian schemes. For any $Q\in D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},k)$, Step 3, these two adjunctions, Step 6, and Step 7 give the following natural bijections (each Hom is in the displayed ordinary coefficient category):
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k_Z)}(Q,H_Z\omega_{Z,A})
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_Z)}(U_ZQ,a_{Z,A}^{\times}A_s)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_s)}(Ra_{!,A}U_ZQ,A_s)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(A_s)}(U_sRa_{!,k}Q,A_s)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k_s)}(Ra_{!,k}Q,H_sA_s)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k_s)}(Ra_{!,k}Q,k_s)\\
&\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{D(k_Z)}(Q,\omega_{Z,k}).
\end{aligned}$$
Apply [lem-galois-yoneda-fully-faithful] in $D(k_Z)$ to this natural isomorphism of representable presheaves and to its inverse. The resulting two representing arrows are inverse because their composites induce the identity presheaf transformations. Thus $H_Z\omega_{Z,A}\cong\omega_{Z,k}$ in $D(k_Z)$. By Step 2 this is exactly the first claimed isomorphism, with its precomposition $k$-action.

source.place: Tag 001P (lemma-yoneda); agent application to the explicitly displayed ordinary compact-support/coefficient adjunction chain

proof.text:
Apply Step 4 with $T=Z$, $L=M$ and $N=\omega_{Z,A}$. Compose with the image under $U_ZR\mathcal Hom_{k_Z}(M,-)$ of the isomorphism of Step 8. This yields
$$R\mathcal Hom_A(U_ZM,\omega_{Z,A})\cong U_ZR\mathcal Hom_k(M,H_Z\omega_{Z,A})\cong U_ZR\mathcal Hom_k(M,\omega_{Z,k}),$$
as an isomorphism in $D(Z_{\mathrm{et}},A)$. Functoriality of the derived internal Hom [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] and the naturality in Step 4 show that this is natural contravariantly in $M$. All computations used K-injective targets and arbitrary source complexes. Therefore there is no boundedness, constructibility or finite-Tor hypothesis on $M$.
